title: Structural basis of competitive recognition of p53 and MDM2 by HAUSP/USP7: implications for the regulation of the p53-MDM2 pathway

grounded.evidence_quote: HAUSP specifically deubiquitinates both p53 and MDM2, to unknown effect.
HAUSP specifically deubiquitinates both p53 and MDM2, to unknown effect.
In normal cells, p53 is maintained at a low level mainly through MDM2-mediated ubiquitylation and subsequent degradation [7–9].
The C-terminal RING-finger motif of MDM2 not only promotes p53 ubiquitylation [10,15], but also targets MDM2 itself for auto-ubiquitylation and subsequent degradation [10,15].

grounded.context: review statement citing other work on transcriptional regulation
grounded.evidence_quote: The MDM2 gene is a transcriptional target of p53 [17–19], so activation of the MDM2 gene by p53 would lead to repression of p53 activity.
Expression of HAUSP was shown to stabilize p53 in vivo and to promote p53-dependent apoptosis and cell-growth arrest [24].

grounded.context: both in vivo and in vitro, cited from other work
grounded.evidence_quote: HAUSP can deubiquitylate MDM2, both in vivo and in vitro, and is required for the stability of MDM2 in normal cells [26–28].
